issues.reason: Daily output exceeds the declared 100-row cap; explicitly bound the report in question and reference before freeze.
AVG(DATE) coerces YYYYMMDD numerically. A mean calendar date requires TO_DAYS, averaging, defined whole-day rounding and FROM_DAYS.
LEFT JOIN COUNT(*) counts an unmatched user as one order. Use COUNT(order_id). Make first/last and payment scope explicitly valid orders.
AVG of NULL joined counts excludes zero-order customers. The stated customer population requires COALESCE(count,0) before AVG; clarify payment counts also refer to valid orders.
A registration-date Top-100 needs an explicit ID tie-break. Case65 also omits the question's order-date < reference-date filter.

Reference uses reference-date minus first-order date instead of last-order minus first-order; ratio-of-sums instead of per-customer mean; excludes zero-order customers; ambiguous registration-day inclusion. Rewrite reference and make authored denominator convention explicit.
Six projected columns violate the predeclared maximum of five. Resolve the draft projection before freeze, preserving the business task and logging the change.
Check and explicitly expose a stable dimension/ID tie-break where a sorted limit or rounded ranking metric has ties. Do not rely on hidden order in scoring.
Question must specify ordering by the displayed rounded rate if the reference orders on its rounded alias, rather than an unrounded rate with different tie membership.
Specify population standard deviation; unqualified standard deviation could mean sample or population.

PERCENT_RANK >= 0.5 chooses an upper-middle observation and returns NULL for a singleton, not an ordinary median. Remove implementation hints and compute a real median using both middle ranks; retain full-group MIN/MAX.
The question says before 2026-09-12; the draft SQL uses <=. Align the boundary without changing reference date.
Sales quantity is for valid orders under the contract. Both concentration CTEs omit the orders join/status filter.

A direct product/item join weights catalogue average price by item frequency. Define and separately aggregate product-grain mean catalogue price and line-grain mean quantity for valid orders. Preserve the >5 mean-quantity threshold even if the result is empty.
The reference omits the question's active-product filter. Bound the relative interval with the fixed reference date.
State the authored inclusive 30-calendar-day interval explicitly as 2026-08-14 through 2026-09-12; distinguish it from the default DATE_SUB(reference,30 DAY) wording.
Make all refund statuses explicit for the authored all-record reason counts; no approved-only condition should be invented.
Refund order count is COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), not refund-record count. Monetary sums remain record-grain approved refunds.
Make approved-refund-order population explicit for both counts and amounts.
Refund join duplicates order paid amounts and order counts. Pre-aggregate refunds per order; specify the refunded-valid-order cohort, per-record average refund and one paid amount per order.
Unqualified last30days follows the existing DATE_SUB(reference,30 DAY) rule; the raw reference starts one day later. Use the contract boundary, not a revised business rule.
Denominator is all approved refund money as worded, not only approved refunds attached to valid orders; use an independent denominator subquery.
State that WeChat/Alipay are combined into a single group, not two separately projected counts.

empty_result_policy: Do not remove, change thresholds, or reject questions just because their reference result is zero/empty/NULL. Case71's quantity >10 and case87's mean quantity >5 are retained as authored.
